projects.title: SMD Dashboard
projects.summary: A project management and analytics dashboard that tracks projects, revenue and client activity in one place.

image.alt: SMD Dashboard, a project management and analytics dashboard home

overview: SMD Dashboard is a project management and analytics dashboard designed for agencies and software teams. Tracking projects, revenue, support tickets and client activity usually means jumping between spreadsheets, chat threads and invoicing tools, so nobody sees the full picture in one place.

I built one clear workspace that brings it together: live stat cards, a 12-month revenue chart, a project pipeline with status and progress, and a recent activity feed. Every number is readable at a glance, and the layout stays clean on both desktop and mobile.
The interface is fast and simple on purpose. It uses reusable components and a consistent design system, so new views and reports can be added quickly without redesigning the page.
projects.role: I worked as the full-stack developer on this project. I designed the interface, built the front end, set up the data layer and APIs behind the dashboard, and handled the deployment.
projects.resultsIntro: A demo build showing how SMD Lab designs and ships product interfaces.

results.label: months of revenue tracked in the chart

projects.title: Delight Kitchen
projects.summary: A website for a Nigerian kitchen serving freshly prepared meals, built so customers can see the menu and order in seconds.

image.alt: The Delight Kitchen website, built for a Nigerian kitchen serving freshly prepared meals

overview: Delight Kitchen prepares authentic Nigerian meals fresh every day. Their old online presence made customers hunt for the menu and had no simple way to order, so many hungry visitors left before placing an order.

The new website keeps everything clear and fast. A mouth-watering hero, a clean menu, and an easy Order Now button are always within reach. Food photography is compressed and served in responsive sizes, so the page loads quickly on a phone, even on a slow connection.
Everything is built to turn visits into orders: simple navigation, readable prices, delivery information up front, and a layout that works as well on mobile as on desktop.
projects.role: I designed and built the website, optimised the food photography for fast loading, and set up the deployment. I also wrote the copy with Delight Kitchen so each dish is described clearly, from ingredients to delivery details.

projects.title: Software Dashboard
projects.summary: An internal dispatch tool for a logistics team coordinating two hundred daily routes.
overview: Dispatchers were running the day from a wall of paper and a phone. The tool had to be usable at speed, with one hand, in a depot that is too loud to think in.

Vector Ops puts the whole day on one screen: every route, its current state, and the two exceptions that actually need a decision. Colour is reserved for those exceptions and used nowhere else, so anything red means stop.
It is keyboard-first throughout. A dispatcher can move a route, reassign a driver and close a job without lifting their hands off the keys.
projects.role: I designed the interface against a week of observation in the depot, built the front end, and wrote the keyboard model. I ran the usability sessions that settled the exception rules.

projects.title: The Real Reason Why Humans Started Wearing Clothes
projects.summary: Stickman explainer videos for a YouTube channel, edited and animated from script to final cut.

image.alt: A stickman caveman in front of a cave and campfire, why clothes?

overview: Ink Explainer is a YouTube channel that explains big ideas through stickman animation. Each video turns a complex topic, like what life was really like for ancient humans, into a clear, funny and easy-to-follow story that holds attention from the first second.

I edit and animate the videos from script to final cut. That covers pacing, stickman character animation, sound design, captions and thumbnails, all built around a consistent visual style so every episode feels like part of the same channel.
Because the style and workflow are repeatable, new episodes can be produced quickly without losing quality, which helps the channel keep a steady upload schedule.
projects.role: I handled the video editing, stickman animation, sound design, thumbnails and final export, working from the channel's scripts.

projects.title: SMD Brand Identity
projects.summary: A full identity for a roastery: wordmark, packaging system, and a sign that reads from the road.
overview: Northbound roast coffee for sale at markets and in two small shops. The identity had to survive a hand-written chalkboard, a kraft bag, and a shopfront seen from a moving car.

The wordmark is drawn for distance — wide, low, and unambiguous at the size a customer sees it first. The packaging system is built so a new origin is a colour swap and a label change, not a redesign.
The shopfront sign was the hardest test. It is one flat colour, one cut shape, and it had to be legible in rain.
projects.role: I drew the identity, built the packaging system, and art-directed the photography. I also wrote the print specifications so the roastery can order directly without us in the loop.
